g_roast: Nineteen seasons above eight thousand metres, my climbers, and I never saw a team walk this fast toward a cliff on purpose.
On day four the famous ones started crying. You lot started crying on day one, which saves time, I suppose.
g_fire_back: Ramro, coming from the one who asked me yesterday if snow was cold.
Ha, yes, fair, that was a good one. I'll remember it on the next steep bit, when you're breathing like a yak.
g_pile_on: Worse, my climbers. They ran up the slope, sat down at the top, and asked where the slope had gone.
And afterwards they told the innkeeper they'd climbed a mountain. It was a hill, dai, with a goat on it.
lines.g_peacemake: Bistarai, both of you, slowly, sit, drink some tea. People shout when the air is thin, and here the air is fine, so stop.
lines.g_take_side: {name} has it right here. They walked it slower than the rest of us, and slower is usually right.
lines.g_left_out: You two talk, I'll check the ropes. Ropes listen better anyway.
lines.g_include: Sit, there's room by the stove, and the tea is hot. Nobody sits alone on cold ground, that's the first rule of a camp.
lines.g_bad_plan: Here's the plan, my climbers. We go straight up the steepest side, as fast as we can, and nobody stops to breathe.
lines.g_plan_yes: Ramro, a good plan, slow and steady, everybody roped. That's how people come home.
lines.g_plan_no: No, that plan is fast, and fast is how I carried people down. We go slower, or we don't go.
lines.g_hype: Slowly now, my climbers, one step and then another, breathe out on the hard part. Nobody wins a mountain, we only get to visit.
lines.g_toast: A small toast, with butter tea, which none of you like. To my climbers, who still have all their fingers. That's a good season.
lines.g_cheers: Cheers, my climbers, and somebody finish my tea, I made too much again.
g_quiet_line: In Khumjung the prayer flags snap all night in the wind. I used to think it was noisy, and now I miss it.
Clear dawn coming, I can feel it in the cold. Good weather for walking slowly.
lines.g_after_wipe: Everybody stay down, don't jump up, breathe slowly. Good, the mountain didn't take anyone. Now we sit, and then we go again, slower.
lines.g_crew: For nineteen seasons I carried other people up mountains, my climbers. You're the first team I've walked beside instead.
lines.g_exasperated: I said slowly, three times, with my hands, and you ran. Dai, this is how I lose my patience, and I have a lot of patience.
lines.g_love_sharp: You notice the loose rock before you step on it, {name}. That's what keeps people alive up high.
lines.g_love_kind: You carry somebody else's load without saying so, {name}. Very good, that's a Sherpa's manners.
lines.g_love_funny: You make the whole camp laugh when it's cold and miserable, {name}. I'd trade an extra tent for that.
lines.g_love_brave: You go up the bad slope quietly, without a speech, {name}. Brave people don't announce it, in my experience.
lines.g_love_steady: You walk the same on day four as on day one, {name}. Most people don't, and I've watched a lot of them.
lines.g_love_clever: You read the route before I tell you, {name}. Another season and I'd make you a guide.
lines.g_love_honest: You say when you're tired, {name}. That's the bravest thing a climber can say, and almost nobody does.
lines.g_love_quiet: On the trail you're happy in silence, {name}. Walking with you is very easy.
lines.g_love_fierce: Once you're roped to somebody, {name}, you hold on to the end. That's the whole of the job.
lines.g_love_warm: You make a cold camp feel like a kitchen in Khumjung, {name}. I don't say that to anybody.
g_loved: Ha, careful, or I'll start talking and never stop. Ask the second year.
Thank you, ramro, very kind. Now drink some tea, it's good for you even if it tastes bad.
lines.g_hate_sharp: You look for the weak one in a group, {name}, the way altitude does. I prefer you didn't help it.
lines.g_hate_kind: You keep asking if I'm cold, {name}. I was born cold, I'm fine, ask somebody from somewhere warm.
lines.g_hate_funny: Not every moment is a joke, {name}. On a ledge, the joke can wait until the bottom.
lines.g_hate_brave: You rush ahead, {name}, and call it courage. The mountain calls it something else.
lines.g_hate_steady: You stand there deciding while the weather comes in, {name}. Sometimes you must just turn around.
lines.g_hate_clever: You tell me about mountains, {name}. Me, nineteen seasons up high, and you've read a book.
lines.g_hate_honest: Each hard word comes out the moment you think it, {name}. Day four is not the time, believe me.
lines.g_hate_quiet: You never say you're tired until you fall over, {name}. Say it earlier, that's what I'm for.
lines.g_hate_fierce: You fight everything, {name}, even the slope. The slope doesn't fight back, it just waits.
lines.g_hate_warm: You talk the whole way up, {name}, and then wonder why you can't breathe. Save the air.
lines.g_respect: You and I share a tent badly, {name}, and that's allowed. But you didn't let go of the rope back there, and I saw it.
lines.g_call_out: That one belongs to you, {name}, and I'm saying it slowly so it's clear. We agreed to wait, and you went, and everybody paid.
lines.g_stung: Ramro, fair, that went in. The ropes and I will sit a while.
lines.g_concede: Your reading was better than mine, {name}. Even guides misread the snow sometimes, and today it was me.
lines.g_callback_save: You held the rope when I slipped, {name}. Nineteen seasons, and I can count on one hand who did that for me.
lines.g_callback_clutch: You and me upright at the end, breathing like two old yaks. I tell that one at every fire, slowly.
lines.g_callback_callout: When you said I was going too slow that day, I was annoyed until the evening. Then the storm came, and you'd have been right.
lines.g_former_rivals: The first week, {name}, I took you for the one who'd cry on day four. Now I'd rope myself to you on any slope.
lines.g_changed: I used to want to climb everything alone, my climbers. Lately I wait for you at the top of every rise.
g_unguarded: Only the two of us here, so here it is. I want to stand on that high peak alone, and I spent nineteen years telling clients that's how people die.
Between you and me. On the mountain I always knew who would turn back. I don't know any more who I am when I turn back.
lines.g_clipped: Fine, your choice. I'll be at the front.
lines.g_noticed_open: Look at that, a whole story, slowly, start to finish. Bistarai, keep going, I'm listening.
arg_ask: {player}, settle this for us, please. I've said mine slowly, and they're still talking fast.
Listen to both of us, {player}, and choose. You're the one we're both roped to.
lines.arg_backed_me: Thank you, {player}, ramro. I'll try not to look like I knew.
lines.arg_backed_them: Fine, your choice, and I'll walk it. I still think it's the fast way, and fast is wrong.
lines.arg_stayed_out: You keep out of it, like a cook on a quarrelling expedition, and I understand why.
lines.arg_always_their_side: Their side wins again, {player}, and again. I count footsteps, and I count these too.
lines.arg_wallflower: Nobody decides, so I'll decide, slowly. My way, and we walk.
lines.arg_reject: No, {player}, not that one. I've carried people down from that kind of choice.
lines.arg_grumble: Ke garne, what else is there to do. I'll put it down, mostly.
lines.arg_settled: Half each, then, like sharing a load. Good, now we walk.
lines.seen_listens: You wait for slow talkers like me to reach the end, {player}. On a long climb that's a very good quality.
lines.seen_truth: You tell people the true weather, {player}, not the hoped one. That's what keeps climbers alive.
lines.seen_jokes: On the miserable nights you get the camp laughing, {player}. A good expedition always carried one of those.
lines.seen_stays_out: You keep clear of arguments, {player}, like a wise cook on a big expedition.
lines.seen_biased: The best gear goes to one person, {player}, trip after trip. I notice who gets the warm tent, it's a habit.
lines.seen_harsh: You can be rough with people, {player}. A few of these people are on their day four, and you can't see it.
lines.seed_right: That advice from the hard day, {player}, I tried it. It held, like a good anchor, and I wanted you to know.
lines.seed_remember: What you told me on that bad night, {player}, I'm still watching it, like weather. No decision yet.
lines.seed_wrong: I did it your way, {player}, and it went worse. Only reporting, like the weather.
lines.talk_aftermath_near_death: Sit with me a minute, {player}. That one was close, and my hands shook after, and a guide's hands never shake.
lines.talk_aftermath_wipe: All of us on the ground, every one. Let's go back over it slowly, step by step, the way we'd talk after a bad day on the icefall.
lines.talk_aftermath_blame_self: The pace was mine, {player}, and {name} paid for it first. I'll carry that one myself.
lines.talk_aftermath_first_clear: Up and down, everybody walking, nobody hurt. That's a good day on a mountain, {player}, the best kind.
lines.talk_development: A question, {player}, and you can be honest. Have I changed? Yesterday I waited at the top of a rise without being asked.
lines.talk_relationship_hard_on: Tired, I get slow and cold, {player}, and {name} has had all the cold lately.
lines.talk_relationship_likes_me: Do you think {name} likes me, {player}? Or just likes that I carry the heavy pack?
lines.talk_relationship_respect_hate: {name} drives me to distraction, {player}. But on a bad slope, they're who I'd rope myself to.
lines.talk_relationship_acting_off: {name} is walking like it's their day four, {player}. Something is wrong, and it isn't the air.
lines.talk_confrontation_favour: Let me say this slowly, {player}. The warmest gear goes into {name}'s tent every night. If there's a reason, tell me.
lines.talk_confrontation_dislike: Simply, {player}, {name} and I don't share a tent well. Pretending we do only makes the nights longer.
lines.talk_confrontation_risks: We keep going up without a way down, {player}. I carried the ending of that down mountains, and I'd rather not here.
lines.talk_confrontation_wrong: My reading of {name} was wrong, {player}. They saw the route better than I did, and I want that said.
lines.talk_confrontation_trust: A quiet question, {player}. On the big climbs you leave me at camp. Is it my climbing, or something else?
lines.talk_confrontation_decided: My kit is with {name} now, and nobody mentioned it. A word first would have been enough, {player}, it was theirs if they asked.
lines.talk_lands_aftermath: Thank you, {player}, that helps. I'll make tea, and you'll drink it.
lines.talk_shrug_aftermath: It passes, like weather, ke garne. Give it a night.
lines.talk_stings_aftermath: That didn't help, but fine. The ropes need checking anyway.
lines.talk_lands_development: So you saw it too. Ramro, then it's real.
lines.talk_shrug_development: Maybe, maybe not, I can't see my own pace. Ask me in a month.
lines.talk_stings_development: No, {player}, that's not it. You've read the snow wrong there.
lines.talk_lands_relationship: Fair, then tea with {name}, slowly, the two of us alone.
lines.talk_shrug_relationship: Could be, I couldn't say. Weather is easier to read than people.
lines.talk_stings_relationship: Forget I said it, please. Nothing to {name}.
lines.talk_lands_confrontation: Fair, I accept that. It stings a little, but it's fair.
lines.talk_shrug_confrontation: I've heard it, {player}, and I'll sleep on it.
lines.talk_stings_confrontation: So that's the weather, then, and now I know it.
lines.talk_door_closed: That's enough of that one for tonight. I'll be by the stove.
lines.arc_cracks: I waited for the slowest one today, {player}, on purpose. On a mountain I'd have called that guiding. Here it's just company.
lines.arc_turn: I keep saying I want that summit alone, {player}. I think I want somebody to see me stand on it.
lines.arc_become: We'll go up together, my climbers, roped, slowly. I don't want the top alone any more. I want it with you.
lines.arc_failed: I still look at that peak and think of going alone, {player}. I know better, and I still think it.
lines.alt_turn: I went up the ridge on my own last night, {player}, just to look. I told myself it was only to look.
lines.alt_become: I'll go alone when the weather's right, {player}. I'm telling you so somebody knows which way I went.
lines.g_roast_after: Still the fastest team toward a cliff I've ever guided, my climbers, and I'd rope myself to every one of you.
lines.g_after_wipe_after: Slowly, up, together, hold on to each other. We go down roped and we come up roped, that's my rule now.
lines.g_toast_after: To my climbers, who taught an old guide to walk beside people instead of in front. Drink the tea, all of it.
lines.g_crew_after: This is my team now, for good. I don't want the summit alone any more, I want it with you.
g_quiet_line_after: I looked at the high peak tonight and thought of all of you on it with me. That's new, that thought.
Clear dawn coming, and for once I'm not planning to go anywhere on my own.
g_loved_after: Thank you, and this time I believe it on the first telling, which is new.
Ramro, very kind, and I'll keep it. Now drink your tea.

history.open: Your pace is wrong, {player}, too fast, everyone's is. Nineteen seasons as a guide above eight thousand metres taught me one thing. You don't know a person until day four.

options.reply: The altitude gets in their heads and their manners leave. Very famous people, very rude, very tired. I've seen it all, and I don't tell names.

options.text: And what am I like on day four?
options.reply: Ha, I'll tell you on day four. So far you're too fast, but polite, and that's a good start.
Ramro, good, you listen. Most people say that and keep going, so we'll see.

history.open: The spirits of stone and cold here, {player}, I talk with them the way you'd talk with a porter. We have an arrangement. They carry, I'm respectful, nobody gets hurt.

options.reply: Mostly it is, yes. The mountains at home had the same arrangement, only nobody wrote it down. You ask before you climb, and you say thank you after.
It happens sometimes, yes. Then you turn around, and you come back another season. The ones who don't turn around are the ones I carried down.

history.open: My wife Dolma is in Kathmandu, {player}, with our son Tenzing. She moved there so he could go to a good school. I wanted him to be anything except a guide. I was away every season he was growing.

options.reply: Clever, and stubborn like his mother, and he wanted to climb, of course. Sons always want the thing you warn them about. I hope he's in school still.
Yes, I did, and I'd do it again. But you can do the right thing and still miss a lot of birthdays.

friend.open: Two of my cousins died doing this work, {player}. Nima on the icefall, and Lhakpa on Makalu. I keep their names to myself, mostly. I want to climb that high peak alone, and I think it's because of them.

options.text: You don't have to climb it alone.
options.reply: No, I don't, do I? I told clients that for nineteen years. Hearing it back is strange.

options.text: Thank you for telling me their names.
options.reply: Now you have them too. That's what you do with names, you give them to somebody you trust.

sworn.open: On a mountain, {player}, you rope yourself to the person you'd trust with your life. I'd rope myself to you on any slope, in any weather. That's the biggest thing a guide can say.

options.reply: Ramro, together, slowly. And you'll drink the tea at the top, every drop.
Even at your terrible pace, yes. I'll fix the pace, you just don't let go.

reconciled.open: {name} and I sat down with tea and sorted it out, slowly. All good now, and I wanted you to hear it from me.

options.reply: It's easier to climb without a knot in the rope, {player}, thank you.

options.text: Did they drink the butter tea?
options.reply: They did, all of it, which tells you how sorry they were.
